chain_of_thought:
First, analyze the geometry and loading of the truss. It is an equilateral truss with a load P = 50.0 kN applied exactly at the apex (Node C). 
Due to symmetry, the reaction forces at the supports should be equal. 
Sum of moments about A: $50 \text{ kN} \times (L/2) - R_{By} \times L = 0$. This gives $R_{By} = 25.0 \text{ kN}$ (upwards).
Sum of forces in Y: $R_{Ay} + R_{By} - 50 = 0$, giving $R_{Ay} = 25.0 \text{ kN}$ (upwards).
Sum of forces in X: $R_{Ax} = 0$.
The student calculated $R_{Ay} = 75.00 \text{ kN}$ and $R_{By} = -25.00 \text{ kN}$, which implies a downward reaction at B and an abnormally high upward reaction at A. This indicates an error in their global equilibrium equations in Step 1.
explanation_to_student: Take a closer look at your global statics in Step 1. Because the equilateral truss is perfectly symmetrical and the 50 kN load is applied exactly in the middle at the apex, the load should be distributed equally between the two supports. Therefore, both $R_{Ay}$ and $R_{By}$ should be 25.0 kN pointing upwards. It looks like you might have made a sign error in your sum of moments equation which resulted in a downward reaction at B. Correcting the support reactions will fix the rest of your joint force calculations!
